currentContext.strengths: Leading/2nd-largest positions across multiple North American niches: leading radiopharmaceuticals manufacturer, 2nd-largest US radiopharmacy network (~20% volume market share), 2nd-largest US allergenic extract player and sole US supplier of venom immunotherapy, leading mid-sized sterile-injectables CDMO in North America|In-house API manufacturing, strong supply-chain management and onshore Montreal manufacturing support the Radiopharma business|Strong customer stickiness in CDMO: top 10 customers associated for over five years with a 92% repeat business rate; products distributed across 140+ countries|Innovation leadership in cardiac PET imaging via differentiated Ruby-Fill® product with longer generator life, better image quality/consistency and no additional shielding capex versus Fluorine-18 agents|Trusted, century-old HollisterStier Allergy brand serving 2,000+ allergists and physicians|CRDMO track record of 85+ integrated drug discovery programs, serving 8 of the top 20 global pharma companies, with rising large-pharma revenue mix (under 5% in FY2023 to over 36% in FY2026)
currentContext.strategies: Vision 2030: double consolidated revenue over FY2024, improve EBITDA margins to 23-25%, reduce net debt to zero and raise RoCE to high-teens by FY2030, executed through business-specific growth levers.|Radiopharma: sustain leadership in cardiac PET imaging through Ruby-Fill® (value engineering incl. an AI-enabled 3D cardiac blood flow quantification system), launch MIBG for paediatric neuroblastoma, and expand the PET/SPECT pipeline via new product launches from FY2028.|Radiopharma supply resilience: reduce dependence on the single CMO Montreal site by qualifying an alternate CMO for SPECT products and transitioning development activities to a diversified third-party CMO network.|Radiopharmacy: expand PET pharmacies from three to nine sites and increase presence in Ga-68 PSMA generator-based PET products distributed through SPECT pharmacies to build long-term contracted, high-margin revenue.|CDMO Sterile Injectables: transform Jubilant HollisterStier from a traditional small-molecule contract manufacturer into a specialised biologics-focused CDMO serving complex, higher-value products, via Spokane Line 3/Line 4 capacity addition and a new Montreal Line 5.|CRDMO: integrate the drug discovery, CDMO and API businesses under the single Jubilant Biosys entity (following the API business transfer) to drive operational synergy and grow the higher-margin custom manufacturing/CDMO revenue mix; add large pharma customers and expand European biologics/ADC capabilities via the Pierre Fabre partnership.|Generics: launch new products in the US via the ANDA pipeline and grow the profitable non-US international business, while ramping Roorkee-facility exports and contract-manufacturing partner supply to the US.|Allergy Immunotherapy: strengthen US leadership in bee-sting allergy treatments and allergenic extracts through scientific differentiation and product quality, and expand internationally through strategic partnerships and broader distribution.|Proprietary Novel Drugs: advance the oncology/auto-immune precision-medicine pipeline (JBI-802 for Essential Thrombocythemia/MPN and JBI-778 for Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma/high-grade Glioma) through ongoing Phase I/II clinical trials.|Enterprise risk mitigation: diversify supplier/manufacturing footprint, maintain US stock buffers, and pursue phased modernisation/replacement capex (incl. a new Liquid/Lyo line) to reduce single-site and ageing-asset dependence.|The Company manages its capital structure to maintain financial flexibility, monitoring a net-debt-to-equity gearing ratio and stating it may adjust dividends paid, return capital to shareholders, issue new shares, or sell assets to reduce debt in order to maintain or adjust that structure. Governance philosophy frames Board oversight of major capital expenditure, acquisitions and divestments as part of its strategic-oversight mandate, and dividend distribution is governed by a published Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations.
currentContext.expansion: Radiopharma: master planning for the Ruby-Fill® manufacturing expansion is complete, expected to be delivered within 24-36 months, alongside capacity doubling through second-shift production; an ongoing USD 50 Million investment is establishing six new PET manufacturing facilities expected to become operational from FY2028, supported by a new Theranostics Centre of Excellence in Boston. Radiopharmacy: a USD 60+ Million capex programme (envisaged June 2024) is adding four new SPECT radiopharmacies (first opened in Seattle, March 1, 2026; remaining three due H2 FY2027) and six PET manufacturing facilities (due for completion by H2 FY2028), funded via internal accruals and long-term credit. CDMO Sterile Injectables: a USD 300+ Million Spokane expansion is doubling capacity via two new high-speed (400 vials/minute) isolator-based fill lines with lyophilisers, adding 200,000 sq ft of manufacturing space, partly funded by a USD 149.6 Million BARDA cooperative agreement; Line 3 launched in Q2 FY2026 and is undergoing technology transfers for 10+ products (including one of the world's largest oncology products) with commercial batch production expected from late FY2027 subject to FDA approval; Line 4 is expected to begin technology transfers in FY2027 and commercial production by FY2028. At Montreal, a USD 114 Million Line 5 expansion (isolator technology) is under construction and expected to generate revenue from FY2029, while the existing line runs lean, focused on radiopharmaceuticals, through FY2027-FY2028; the Montreal facility received an OAI classification after a US FDA audit in FY2026 and a warning letter in May 2026, prompting CAPA remediation, strengthened media-fill programs, third-party oversight and new production/quality leadership. CRDMO: capacity is being added in Greater Noida and Bengaluru (potentially doubling revenue) with a new flagship facility planned at Devanahalli, Bengaluru expected to support a fourfold increase in scale over time; during FY2026, Jubilant Biosys launched an integrated Discovery and Scale-Up facility in Noida (reactors 100-250 litres, capable of generating materials from grams to 25 kilograms), established a Compound Management Facility, added automated ADME platforms (~1,000 assays/week, 3-5 day turnaround) and set up six specialised Chemistry Centres of Excellence. Allergy Immunotherapy: expansion of lyophilisation capacity and upgrade of extraction facilities/critical manufacturing equipment. Generics: debottlenecking and GMP enhancement projects at Roorkee.

risks.risk: Product quality and cGMP compliance, acutely evidenced by a US FDA Warning Letter at the Montreal contract manufacturing facility
risks.note: The Montreal facility received a Warning Letter following a US FDA post-audit; this increases regulatory scrutiny and may lead to delays in approvals/filings, supply disruptions to the US market, reduced customer confidence and reputational loss, with prolonged remediation raising the risk of further enforcement action.

The pharmaceutical industry is characterised by intense competition, pricing regulations, reimbursement pressures and tender-based procurement; shifts in prescribing practices, distribution channels or competitive product introductions may adversely affect market share, revenues, margins and returns, particularly in segments with limited pricing flexibility.

The Company depends on third parties for APIs, intermediates, packaging materials, utilities, spares and logistics; supplier quality issues, shortages, transportation constraints, regulatory actions or geopolitical developments could affect production schedules, customer deliveries and costs.

Dependence on a single or limited manufacturing site for specific products or processes increases exposure to localised operational disruptions, equipment breakdowns, utilities failures or regulatory actions, which could adversely affect supply commitments, customer deliveries, revenues and reputation.

Concentration of revenues in a few customers, products or programs exposes the Company to volatility in revenues and capacity utilisation; changes in customer procurement strategies, demand forecasts or pipeline outcomes may result in pricing pressure and under-absorption of fixed costs.

Changes in trade policies, tariffs, duties and export controls across jurisdictions, plus ongoing geopolitical tensions, may increase costs, disrupt supply chains and affect pricing competitiveness and cross-border supply arrangements, particularly for Radiopharma products.

Increasing reliance on digital systems across manufacturing, quality, finance and commercial functions exposes the Company to cyber incidents that could cause unauthorised data access, disruption of operations (including quality release processes) and regulatory non-compliance.

The Company's ability to meet operational, compliance and strategic objectives depends on availability and retention of skilled personnel; attrition, skill shortages or leadership transitions may affect operational continuity and execution of strategic initiatives.

one-line thesis: Jubilant Pharmova delivered 19% Q4 revenue growth driven by Radiopharma and CDMO, but EBITDA margins compressed to 15.7% due to Montreal under-absorption and SPECT supply shortages. The investment thesis hinges on H2FY27 margin recovery as Montreal stabilizes and Line 3 (Spokane) begins commercial production of high-margin biologics, targeting $80-90mn peak revenue.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs.2,290 Cr (+19% YoY); EBITDA: Rs.363 Cr (+2% YoY), Margin 15.7% (-272 bps YoY) due to SPECT shortage & Montreal under-absorption; Normalized PAT: Rs.129 Cr (down YoY on higher depreciation/interest); Order Book: 10+ molecules in tech transfer (Line 3); Net Debt: Rs.1,952 Cr (Target zero by FY30).
guidance: FY27 Revenue: Low double-digit growth; FY27 Margins: H1 pressured (SPECT shortage), H2 recovery to 17-18%; Order Inflow: Line 3 commercial start late FY27; Capex: ~Rs.1,668 Cr (similar to FY26) for Line 4, Line 5, PET pharmacies.
order book & pipeline: 10+ products in tech transfer for Line 3 (80% complex biologics including major oncology asset); Commercial production expected late FY27; Peak revenue for Line 3 projected at $80-90mn.
segment / subsidiary detail: Radiopharma: Margin pressure in H1FY27 due to $14mn SPECT revenue miss; CDMO: Line 3 tech transfer revenue $60-80mn expected in FY27; Allergy: 90% US exposure, growing via share gains & non-US expansion; Generics: Margins expanded to double digits.
growth verticals / optionality: MIBG NDA filing H2FY27 (accelerated review expected); Ruby-Fill annuity model (30%+ growth); PET pharmacy network commercialization starting FY27; European expansion in Allergy.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 Margin 15.7% impacted by Montreal under-absorption and SPECT supply gap; FY27 H1 margins temporarily depressed; H2FY27 margins guided to 17-18% as Montreal stabilizes and Line 3 absorbs costs.
capex / expansion: FY26 Capex Rs.1,668 Cr; FY27 similar level; Key spends: Spokane Line 4 ($34mn pending), Montreal Line 5 ($87mn pending), PET Pharmacies ($50mn pending).
capital allocation: Strict ROCE threshold for investments; No new major capex beyond current pipeline (Lines 3/4/5, PET) for next 12-18 months; Focus on deleveraging from FY28 to achieve net debt zero by FY30.
risks & watch-items: Montreal ramp-up delays extending losses beyond FY28; Regulatory delays in MIBG NDA or PET pharmacy approvals; Sustained SPECT supply chain disruptions; High interest/depreciation burden suppressing PAT.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Transparent about near-term margin headwinds (H1FY27) but confident in H2 recovery and long-term ROCE from biologics/radiopharma assets.
non-obvious takeaways: Montreal losses expected to persist at ~Rs.200 Cr run-rate in FY27 before meaningful reduction in FY28; MIBG priority review voucher status uncertain due to predecessor product (Azedra) history; Ruby-Fill operates on a razor-blade annuity model with 6-7 week replacement cycles.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply shortage of SPECT products and Montreal under-absorption compressing near-term margins | Dr. Reddy's Laboratories | beneficiary | Low | Potential alternative supplier for SPECT components if Jubilant supply remains constrained, though direct overlap is limited. |
| High switching costs and stringent aseptic requirements for complex biologics creating durable CDMO relationships | Divi's Laboratories | beneficiary | Med | Sector-wide tailwind for Indian CDMOs securing complex biologic contracts; validates premium pricing power in sterile injectables. |
| Delays in Montreal profitability and high capex cycle delaying free cash flow generation | Jubilant Pharmova Ltd | loser | High | Self-inflicted near-term pain from Montreal ramp-up and SPECT supply issues delaying margin expansion and deleveraging. |

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and supplies radiopharmaceuticals (PET/SPECT/therapeutic) and operates the second-largest radiopharmacy network in the US; it also runs a sterile fill-finish injectables CDMO (Jubilant HollisterStier) in Spokane (US) and Montreal (Canada), a subcutaneous allergy immunotherapy business, a CRDMO offering integrated drug discovery and API manufacturing (Jubilant Biosys), a Generics business selling solid dosage formulations across 50+ countries, and an early-stage Proprietary Novel Drugs oncology/auto-immune pipeline. It serves pharmaceutical and biotech companies, GPOs, allergists and hospitals across national and international markets.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Radiopharma: Margin pressure in H1FY27 due to $14mn SPECT revenue miss; CDMO: Line 3 tech transfer revenue $60-80mn expected in FY27; Allergy: 90% US exposure, growing via share gains & non-US expansion; Generics: Margins expanded to double digits.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Radiopharma:** Ruby-Fill® (Rb-82 generator, cardiac PET), Tc99m-DTPA, Tc99m-MAA, I-131 HICON®, Tc99m-Gluceptate, Tc99m-Sestamibi, Sulfur Colloid, Tc99m-Exametazime, Tc99m-Mertiatide, Tc99m-MDP, MIBG (I-131, in development)
- **Radiopharmacy:** PYLARIFY® (distributed, PET prostate cancer diagnostic), Neuraceq (distributed), Pluvicto (distributed, Lu-177 prostate cancer therapy), Ga-68 PSMA (distributed)
- **Allergy Immunotherapy:** allergenic extracts (200+), insect venom immunotherapy products (six), Ultrafiltered Dog Hair and Dander Extract
- **CDMO Sterile Injectables:** sterile fill-and-finish injectables (liquid and lyophilized), ophthalmic products (liquids, ointments, creams), ampoules
- **CRDMO:** integrated drug discovery services, APIs (~100, incl. Carbamazepine, Oxcarbazepine, Pinaverium), TrialStat eClinical software platform
- **Generics:** solid dosage formulations across cardiovascular, CNS, gastrointestinal, antibiotics and specialty therapeutic areas
- **Proprietary Novel Drugs:** oncology and auto-immune precision-medicine pipeline (two programs in clinical trials)

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: FY27 Revenue: Low double-digit growth; FY27 Margins: H1 pressured (SPECT shortage), H2 recovery to 17-18%; Order Inflow: Line 3 commercial start late FY27; Capex: ~Rs.1,668 Cr (similar to FY26) for Line 4, Line 5, PET pharmacies.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: MIBG NDA filing H2FY27 (accelerated review expected); Ruby-Fill annuity model (30%+ growth); PET pharmacy network commercialization starting FY27; European expansion in Allergy.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global healthcare demand seen as structurally resilient, driven by ageing populations, rising chronic disease and healthcare expenditure.
- US pharmaceutical market growth (10.5% in 2025 to USD 606 Billion) led by oncology, immunology and endocrinology (diabetes/obesity), though 2026 outlook is more complex given the first major wave of patent cliffs and federal drug-price negotiations.
- Acceleration in the obesity market from oral GLP-1 therapies and semaglutide patent expiries expected to widen access and expand the addressable market.
- New oncology modalities (ADCs, bispecific antibodies, CAR-T, radioligand therapies) expected to grow rapidly through 2030, supporting CRDMO/Proprietary Novel Drugs demand.
- Friendshoring/onshoring trend as tariffs push innovator pharma to shift manufacturing to the US, favouring onshore CDMO capacity such as Spokane and Montreal.
- Sterile injectables industry facing a structural demand-supply gap (McKinsey: 700 Million-unit vial-outsourcing shortfall 2023-2027) due to limited internal capacity, cost-reduction focus and biologics pipeline growth, benefiting CDMO players with proven onshore track records.
- Radiopharmacy industry consolidation (top three US networks hold 70% share) and emerging isotopes (Rb-82, Ga-68, Cu-64, Lu-177, Ac-225, Pb-212) driving new PET imaging/theranostics product development and USP 825 compliance-driven outsourcing to radiopharmacies.
- Radiopharma segment expects negative revenue/EBITDA impact from the SPECT product supply shortage to continue into H1 FY2027, with normalised revenue expected to return by H2 FY2027 as the Montreal CMO stabilises.
- Post-Montreal-stabilisation, EBITDA margins are expected to inch up toward the Vision 2030 target from H2 FY2027 onward.
- CDMO Sterile Injectables to see commercial batch production from Spokane Line 3 technology transfers commence in late FY2027, subject to US FDA approval, supporting a fast revenue ramp.
- Net Debt/EBITDA deliberately moved from 1.1x (March 2025) to 1.3x (March 2026) as the company aggressively commits growth capex.
- Technology transfers for more than 10 products across multiple formats/vial sizes are underway on Spokane Line 3; one of the world's largest oncology products has been onboarded onto Line 3.
- CRDMO large-pharma customer share increased from under 5% of revenue in FY2023 to over 36% in FY2026, reflecting a growing engagement pipeline with global pharma/biotech customers.
- Proprietary Novel Drugs pipeline: JBI-802 Phase I/II trial (Essential Thrombocythemia and other MPNs) showing preliminary rapid, durable dose-dependent platelet normalisation; JBI-778 Phase I trial (Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma and high-grade Glioma) actively enrolling patients.
- Radiopharma new-product pipeline: 7 planned PET/SPECT/therapeutic launches (3 in FY2028, 4 in FY2029) targeting an incremental USD 535 Million TAM.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 Margin 15.7% impacted by Montreal under-absorption and SPECT supply gap; FY27 H1 margins temporarily depressed; H2FY27 margins guided to 17-18% as Montreal stabilizes and Line 3 absorbs costs.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Strict ROCE threshold for investments; No new major capex beyond current pipeline (Lines 3/4/5, PET) for next 12-18 months; Focus on deleveraging from FY28 to achieve net debt zero by FY30.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Radiopharma: master planning for the Ruby-Fill® manufacturing expansion is complete, expected to be delivered within 24-36 months, alongside capacity doubling through second-shift production; an ongoing USD 50 Million investment is establishing six new PET manufacturing facilities expected to become operational from FY2028, supported by a new Theranostics Centre of Excellence in Boston. Radiopharmacy: a USD 60+ Million capex programme (envisaged June 2024) is adding four new SPECT radiopharmacies (first opened in Seattle, March 1, 2026; remaining three due H2 FY2027) and six PET manufacturing facilities (due for completion by H2 FY2028), funded via internal accruals and long-term credit. CDMO Sterile Injectables: a USD 300+ Million Spokane expansion is doubling capacity via two new high-speed (400 vials/minute) isolator-based fill lines with lyophilisers, adding 200,000 sq ft of manufacturing space, partly funded by a USD 149.6 Million BARDA cooperative agreement; Line 3 launched in Q2 FY2026 and is undergoing technology transfers for 10+ products (including one of the world's largest oncology products) with commercial batch production expected from late FY2027 subject to FDA approval; Line 4 is expected to begin technology transfers in FY2027 and commercial production by FY2028. At Montreal, a USD 114 Million Line 5 expansion (isolator technology) is under construction and expected to generate revenue from FY2029, while the existing line runs lean, focused on radiopharmaceuticals, through FY2027-FY2028; the Montreal facility received an OAI classification after a US FDA audit in FY2026 and a warning letter in May 2026, prompting CAPA remediation, strengthened media-fill programs, third-party oversight and new production/quality leadership. CRDMO: capacity is being added in Greater Noida and Bengaluru (potentially doubling revenue) with a new flagship facility planned at Devanahalli, Bengaluru expected to support a fourfold increase in scale over time; during FY2026, Jubilant Biosys launched an integrated Discovery and Scale-Up facility in Noida (reactors 100-250 litres, capable of generating materials from grams to 25 kilograms), established a Compound Management Facility, added automated ADME platforms (~1,000 assays/week, 3-5 day turnaround) and set up six specialised Chemistry Centres of Excellence. Allergy Immunotherapy: expansion of lyophilisation capacity and upgrade of extraction facilities/critical manufacturing equipment. Generics: debottlenecking and GMP enhancement projects at Roorkee.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; Transparent about near-term margin headwinds (H1FY27) but confident in H2 recovery and long-term ROCE from biologics/radiopharma assets.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Leading/2nd-largest positions across multiple North American niches: leading radiopharmaceuticals manufacturer, 2nd-largest US radiopharmacy network (~20% volume market share), 2nd-largest US allergenic extract player and sole US supplier of venom immunotherapy, leading mid-sized sterile-injectables CDMO in North America
- In-house API manufacturing, strong supply-chain management and onshore Montreal manufacturing support the Radiopharma business
- Strong customer stickiness in CDMO: top 10 customers associated for over five years with a 92% repeat business rate; products distributed across 140+ countries
- Innovation leadership in cardiac PET imaging via differentiated Ruby-Fill® product with longer generator life, better image quality/consistency and no additional shielding capex versus Fluorine-18 agents
- Trusted, century-old HollisterStier Allergy brand serving 2,000+ allergists and physicians
- CRDMO track record of 85+ integrated drug discovery programs, serving 8 of the top 20 global pharma companies, with rising large-pharma revenue mix (under 5% in FY2023 to over 36% in FY2026)

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Montreal ramp-up delays extending losses beyond FY28; Regulatory delays in MIBG NDA or PET pharmacy approvals; Sustained SPECT supply chain disruptions; High interest/depreciation burden suppressing PAT.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Montreal losses expected to persist at ~Rs.200 Cr run-rate in FY27 before meaningful reduction in FY28; MIBG priority review voucher status uncertain due to predecessor product (Azedra) history; Ruby-Fill operates on a razor-blade annuity model with 6-7 week replacement cycles.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Vision 2030: double consolidated revenue over FY2024, improve EBITDA margins to 23-25%, reduce net debt to zero and raise RoCE to high-teens by FY2030, executed through business-specific growth levers.
- Radiopharma: sustain leadership in cardiac PET imaging through Ruby-Fill® (value engineering incl. an AI-enabled 3D cardiac blood flow quantification system), launch MIBG for paediatric neuroblastoma, and expand the PET/SPECT pipeline via new product launches from FY2028.
- Radiopharma supply resilience: reduce dependence on the single CMO Montreal site by qualifying an alternate CMO for SPECT …
